page.layout: One printed page, single text column; no marginal notes on the left; a short line of signatures ("§ §") below the text. Running head at top centre above the text.

main_text.l: doctis,atque reipsa,non nomine tenus studiosis,et
praeceptoribus meis cum primis gratis et acceptis:
quibus cum de studiis aliisque rebus iucunde vtiliterque
colloquor.
XX. Professores quoque non raro accedo: atque
inde verum esse experior illud, quod quadam in epi-
stola Seneca scribit: nullam rem magis honesta in-
ducere dubios; et in prauum inclinatos ad rectum
revocare, quam bonorum virorum cōuersationem:
frequenter audiri atque aspici paulatim in pectora
descendere praeceptiq; vim obtinere: esse deniq; ali-
quid, quod ex magno viro, vel tacente, quis discat.
XXI. Familiaritati et amicitiae quorundam ego
renunciaui, propterea quod ἰαππῶν pater scri-
pserat, vt eos mufos facerem: ne mea haec in re ter-
giuersatio aliquam ei suspicionem moueret.
XXII. Tandem non statim a coena, sed vnius ad
minimum horae spatio interposito, et recreatiuncu-
lis adhibitis honestis, in cubiculum me cum confero,
antequam quieti me ac somno dedam, memor illius:
Non prius in dulcem declinat lumina somnum
Omnia quàm longi reputauerit acta diei.
quid eo die audierim, legerim, viderim cogito.
XXIII. Et vt boni patresfamilias accepti atq;
expensi habere tabulas solent: ita ephemerides ego
et volumina habeo, in quae obseruatu digna refero.
XXIIII. Tandem sacrorum bibliorum lectio-
ne piisq; ad Deum votis diem claudo.

page.notes: Signature "§ §" at foot is a printed gathering-style mark, not a catchword. Greek word "ἰαππῶν" in XXI is printed as "Ἰαππῶν"-like form ("διαπ..."); transcribed as printed as far as legible; uncertain letters marked. Page-edge shadow and binding are not transcribed. Several words in the first lines are heavily broken by the scan and were read from context: "doctis" (?), "studiis" (?), "rebus" (?). The Greek word in XXI is doubtful: "ἰαππῶν"[?]. Words "mufos" and "obseruatu" follow the print as far as visible.
